OS 410: Foundations of occupational science including the human drive to remain occupied, creation of identity through meaningful activity and enhancing health through occupation will be explored.
OS 420: Habits, routines, roles, and rituals are occupational constructs for occupational science and occupational therapy practice.
OS 430: Exploration of ways individuals and groups create, manage, and shift identities through their choice of and participation in occupations within society.
OS 440: This course delves into the complex nature of occupation and how it contributes to the experience of being human.
OS 450: The capstone Occupational Science course will offer the student time to enhance skills in advanced scholarship, leadership, advocacy, program and policy development, education, or theory development in occupational science and occupational therapy practice.
